section: Linguistic reorganisation demand; Potti Sriramulu's fast and the formation of Andhra State 1953

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the memorial for Potti Sriramulu at Amaravati:
1. It covers 6.80 acres.
2. It was estimated to cost ₹150 crore.
3. Its second phase includes a museum and an auditorium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Amaravati memorial covers 6.80 acres, has an estimated cost of ₹150 crore, and its second phase includes a museum and auditorium.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and component detail separately before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is historically significant because it was regarded as the:
o: first state created by merging all Telugu-speaking regions
first linguistic state formed after Independence
first state formed exclusively on a religious basis
first state formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956
accepted.x: Andhra State was the first state formed on a linguistic basis after Independence and became the precedent for wider reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first linguistic state after Independence from the later nationwide reorganisation of 1956.

accepted.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is commonly described as the “Andhra exception” because it:
o: allowed Madras to become the capital of a separate Andhra State
created a state without any elected legislature
reversed the decision to use language as a basis for state formation
opened the way for the States Reorganisation Commission and nationwide linguistic reorganisation
accepted.x: Although the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee were cautious about linguistic states, the Andhra exception paved the way for the SRC and broader linguistic reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Identify the historical consequence rather than merely recalling the event itself.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of bodies and commissions associated with linguistic reorganisation?
o: JVP Committee → Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Wanchoo Committee → Fazal Ali States Reorganisation Commission
Wanchoo Committee → Dhar Commission → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
Dhar Commission → Wanchoo Committee → JVP Committee → Fazal Ali Commission
accepted.x: The sequence was Dhar Commission in 1948, JVP Committee in 1948–49, Wanchoo in 1953 for Andhra, and the Fazal Ali SRC in 1953–55 for all India.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest commission first and then place the Andhra-specific and all-India bodies.

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission announced on 22 December 1953 was associated with which combination?
o: Fazal Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
K.N. Wanchoo, H.N. Kunzru and Pattabhi Sitaramayya
Fazal Ali, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy and K.M. Panikkar
P.S. Kumaraswami Raja, Fazal Ali and H.N. Kunzru
accepted.x: The SRC was headed by Fazal Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure chairman-member combination and eliminate bodies connected with Andhra alone.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement during 1913–1920 is correct?
o: It began only after the formation of Andhra State in 1953.
It opposed the use of Telugu in education and administration.
It combined demands for an Andhra State, Andhra University, development of Telugu and cultural revival.
It was confined exclusively to the demand for a separate province.
accepted.x: The period 1913–1920 was the propaganda phase, with four broad objectives: Andhra State, Andhra University, Telugu development and cultural revival.
accepted.tq: Prefer the option that captures the full set of objectives rather than an exclusive single-purpose claim.

accepted.s: The first organised Telugu platform that ultimately led towards the formation of Andhra State was associated with which event?
o: The Dhar Commission of 1948
The Wanchoo Committee of 1953
The States Reorganisation Commission of 1953
The Bapatla Andhra Mahasabha of 1913
accepted.x: The Bapatla session of 1913 is regarded as having sown the seeds of the Andhra movement and became the first organised Telugu platform.
accepted.tq: Link the foundational event with the later movement without confusing it with post-Independence commissions.

accepted.s: Bapatla, which played a foundational role in the Andhra movement, is presently the headquarters of which district?
o: Guntur district
Prakasam district
Palnadu district
Bapatla district
accepted.x: Bapatla is the headquarters of Bapatla district.
accepted.tq: Use the exact present administrative association instead of the historical conference association alone.

accepted.s: The annual resolutions and memorandums of the Andhra movement were important mainly because they:
o: transferred the Andhra capital permanently to Hyderabad
replaced the demand for linguistic states with a demand for religious provinces
ended the demand for a separate Andhra province after 1913
kept the Andhra issue on the national agenda until the formation of Andhra State in 1953
accepted.x: Repeated resolutions and memorandums ensured that the Andhra problem remained before national political authorities until Andhra State was formed in 1953.
accepted.tq: Choose the option expressing the cumulative political effect of repeated resolutions.

accepted.s: The district-wise voting adopted at the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session was primarily a response to criticism that the organisation was:
o: controlled by Tamil settlers in Madras
composed mainly of British officials
opposed to the use of Telugu in public life
dominated by Circars and Brahmin interests
accepted.x: Rayalaseema and Nellore leaders criticised the Andhra Mahasabha as a Circars- or Brahmin-led body; district-wise voting was adopted in response.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional change with the specific regional criticism that caused it.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the early milestones of the Andhra movement?
o: Bapatla 1912—first formal resolution; Nidadavolu 1913—first numbered conference; Vijayawada 1914—first Congress session
Nidadavolu 1912—first Andhra Mahasabha; Bapatla 1913—first Congress circle; Vijayawada 1914—first university session
Vijayawada 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first linguistic PCC; Nidadavolu 1914—first Andhra Mahasabha
Nidadavolu 1912—first formal resolution; Bapatla 1913—first numbered Andhra Conference; Vijayawada 1914—first session called Andhra Mahasabha
accepted.x: Nidadavolu in 1912 saw the first formal resolution, Bapatla in 1913 was the first numbered Andhra Conference, and Vijayawada in 1914 was the first session called Andhra Mahasabha.
accepted.tq: Keep the three places and years aligned before comparing the labels attached to them.

accepted.s: The reorganisation of Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines in 1920 was significant because it:
o: fulfilled the Congress’s own organisational promise relating to linguistic units
abolished all provincial Congress committees
placed all Telugu areas under the Madras Provincial Congress Committee
created Andhra State immediately
accepted.x: The 1920 linguistic PCCs reflected the Congress’s own commitment to linguistic organisation, later invoked by the Andhra demand.
accepted.tq: Distinguish organisational reorganisation within Congress from the later creation of constitutional states.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Andhra INC president — Anandacharlu, 1891
First Andhra INC president — Nyapati Subba Rao, 1918
First Andhra Congress Committee president — Anandacharlu, 1891
First Andhra Congress Committee president — Tanguturi Prakasam, 1953
accepted.x: Anandacharlu was the first Andhra INC president in 1891, whereas Nyapati Subba Rao was the first president of the Andhra Congress Committee in 1918.
accepted.tq: Test the two similar leadership titles separately rather than treating them as identical offices.

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains why the Andhra movement was repeatedly slowed before 1953?
o: The immediate acceptance of the Andhra demand by the Central Government
Leadership and regional splits, including Circars–Rayalaseema and Prakasam–Pattabhi divisions
The unanimous opposition of all Telugu-speaking districts to a separate state
The absence of any demand for linguistic organisation within Congress
accepted.x: Factional divisions between regions and leaders, notably Circars versus Rayalaseema and Prakasam versus Pattabhi, repeatedly weakened the movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the internal political cause rather than an absolute or externally imposed explanation.

accepted.s: The provisions of the Sri Bagh Pact continue to be cited particularly in contemporary debates concerning:
o: the status of the Telugu language in the Union List
the creation of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council
the merger of Andhra with Maharashtra
Rayalaseema’s capital, High Court and irrigation concerns
accepted.x: The Sri Bagh terms concerning capital, High Court and irrigation remain important in Rayalaseema-related debates.
accepted.tq: Group the three linked provisions under the region whose interests they addressed.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra University is correct?
o: Its university struggle contributed to the growth of a distinct Telugu intellectual identity.
Its location had no connection with regional political concerns.
It was established only after the formation of Andhra State in 1953.
It was intended exclusively for technical education in Rayalaseema.
accepted.x: The struggle over Andhra University helped build a distinct Telugu intellectual identity and is regarded by many as a forerunner of the Andhra State movement.
accepted.tq: Recognise the broader cultural significance of an institutional demand.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with present-day higher education in Rayalaseema?
o: Central University of Andhra Pradesh — Anantapur
Yogi Vemana University — Kurnool, established in 1953
Central University of Andhra Pradesh — Kadapa, established in 1926
Yogi Vemana University — Amaravati, established after the 2014 Act
accepted.x: The Central University of Andhra Pradesh is located at Anantapur and was set up after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014. Yogi Vemana University is at Kadapa and was established in 2006.
accepted.tq: Check both the location and the institutional history before accepting a match.

accepted.s: The Central University of Andhra Pradesh at Anantapur was set up after which legislation?
o: Andhra University Act, 1925
States Reorganisation Act, 1956
Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
Andhra State Act, 1953
accepted.x: The Central University of Andhra Pradesh, Anantapur, was established after the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the legislation that enabled its establishment.

accepted.s: The death of Potti Sriramulu in the context of the Andhra movement:
o: resulted immediately in the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956
led to the abolition of the Madras Presidency without any further legislation
ended all demands for linguistic reorganisation in India
forced the Central Government to act and helped open the way to the SRC
accepted.x: Potti Sriramulu’s death forced the Centre to respond to the Andhra demand and helped initiate the process that led to the SRC and later reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the immediate political consequence from the later constitutional outcome.

accepted.s: At a tribute event, the historical sequence of capitals associated with Andhra was stated as:
o: Hyderabad → Kurnool → Amaravati
Madras → Amaravati → Kurnool
Kurnool → Hyderabad → Amaravati
Amaravati → Kurnool → Hyderabad
accepted.x: The sequence cited was Kurnool as the capital in 1953, Hyderabad after the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, and Amaravati as the later capital.
accepted.tq: Place the three capitals in their stated historical order rather than by present prominence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the significance of Kurnool becoming the capital of Andhra State in 1953?
o: It was selected after Andhra retained Madras city.
It was selected as the capital of the entire Madras State.
It became the capital because the new state, having lost Madras, had to use the relatively undeveloped town of Kurnool.
It was chosen as the permanent capital under the 1956 States Reorganisation Act.
accepted.x: The loss of Madras left the new Andhra State administratively and economically weak, requiring it to use the relatively undeveloped town of Kurnool as its capital.
accepted.tq: Link the capital choice to the political and economic consequence of losing Madras.

accepted.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 is associated with which provision?
o: Abolition of the statutory concept of a state capital
Affirmation of Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital
Transfer of Andhra Pradesh’s capital to Hyderabad
Recognition of Kurnool as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 affirms Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory effect instead of confusing historical and current capitals.

accepted.s: The Telugu Ganga project was intended to provide irrigation to approximately how much area, along with supplying water to Chennai?
o: 20,000 acres
2.75 lakh acres
5 lakh acres
75,000 acres
accepted.x: Telugu Ganga was intended to irrigate 2.75 lakh acres and provide water to Chennai, although the reported present irrigation reach is much lower.
accepted.tq: Separate the planned command area from the much smaller area reportedly irrigated in practice.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported present performance of the Telugu Ganga project?
o: It has been abandoned because Rayalaseema has no irrigation grievance.
It supplies irrigation only to coastal Andhra and no water to Chennai.
It can barely irrigate about 20,000 acres despite the larger intended command area.
It irrigates nearly 2.75 lakh acres as originally intended.
accepted.x: The project was intended for 2.75 lakh acres and Chennai water supply, but it was reported to be barely irrigating 20,000 acres.
accepted.tq: Compare the intended figure with the reported actual performance.

accepted.s: The panel set up in 2026 in connection with the Gorkhaland statehood demand was headed by:
o: Fazal Ali
Pankaj Kumar Singh
H.N. Kunzru
K.M. Panikkar
accepted.x: The Ministry of Home Affairs set up a panel under Pankaj Kumar Singh to examine the Gorkhaland statehood demand.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the contemporary MHA panel from the historical States Reorganisation Commission members.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 2026 Andhra University centenary observance is correct?
o: The centenary commemorates the period 1926–2026 and was associated with an announcement of ₹500 crore support.
The centenary marked 1913–2026 and announced ₹150 crore for a Potti Sriramulu memorial.
The university was founded in 1953 and the centenary was celebrated at Kurnool.
The centenary programme excluded any proposal for international ranking improvement.
accepted.x: Andhra University’s centenary covers 1926–2026, and the State announced ₹500 crore to help it enter the global top 100.
accepted.tq: Match the centenary period with the correct funding and institutional objective.

accepted.s: Who was credited as the founding Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University during the 2026 centenary observances?
o: Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy
Ramakrishna Rao
Nyapati Subba Rao
Potti Sriramulu
accepted.x: Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy was credited as the founding Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a university office-holder from political leaders associated with the Andhra State movement.

accepted.s: The Andhra University centenary celebrations in 2026 were associated with which chief guest?
o: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan
Governor S. Abdul Nazeer
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu
Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan
accepted.x: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan was the chief guest at the Andhra University centenary observance.
accepted.tq: Separate the chief guest from the Governor and political leaders mentioned in the same observance.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: N. Venkatramayya — first Speaker of Andhra State
C.M. Trivedi — first Governor of Andhra State
Sanjiva Reddy — first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra State
Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy — first Governor of Andhra State
accepted.x: Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy was the founding Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University, not the first Governor of Andhra State. C.M. Trivedi held the latter position.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped office-holder in the otherwise familiar set of pairings.
